direction: Search a symmetry-restricted family from scratch to find a different, intrinsically rigid topology: fix the cyclic group C11 acting on R^13 as five 2D rotation planes with angles 2*pi*k/11 (k=1..5) plus three fixed coordinates, parametrise 9 orbit representatives on S^12 (9*12=108 free variables, generic orbits of size 11 giving exactly 99 points), and optimise the representatives with L-BFGS-B on LogSumExp_alpha of the full generated code with alpha=100 then 400; also try C9 with 11 representatives acting as four rotation planes plus five fixed coordinates. After convergence, release the symmetry, run annealed LogSumExp (alpha 100->600) and then the wide-active LP, and compare against the record by score and by contact-degree sequence; even a symmetric seed 1e-4 worse is valuable if release-plus-polish breaks symmetry into a new rigid basin rather than returning to the 3-hub graph.

Equalise per-point maxima with a scheduled LogSumExp plus std and softplus homotopy optimised by L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients from perturbed and random starts, screened by short LP polish for balanced high-degree contact graphs.
direction: Run an equioscillation homotopy whose explicit goal is to equalise per-point maxima, not just lower the global max: minimise F = LogSumExp_alpha(all pair cosines) + lambda * std_i(per-point-max_i) + mu * mean_i(softplus_alpha(per-point-max_i - global_softmax)) with alpha scheduled 40, 80, 160, 320, 640 and lambda scheduled 1.0 down to 0.05, using L-BFGS-B on unconstrained representatives normalised in the objective (like prior smooth codes but with the per-point penalty and analytic gradients), starting both from best.npy perturbed at sigma=0.01,0.03,0.08 and from 5 fresh random configurations. Keep a candidate only if, after a short Direction-1-style polish, its number of points with at least 5 contacts at tolerance 1e-6 exceeds that of the record (currently essentially zero at 1e-9 and concentrated on 3 points), even if its score is up to 1e-6 worse, because a balanced high-degree basin is the target topology.

idea: Large cluster surgery on the 1e-6 near-contact graph with hole reinsertion, per-point minimax descent, SA acceptance and fingerprint archive to force basin changes.
direction: Do large contact-graph surgery with an anti-return archive instead of worst-1-to-3-point kicks: build the near-contact graph at tolerance 1e-6, pick a connected cluster of 8-15 points (e.g. a hub plus its near-neighbours, or the densest community), delete the whole cluster, and reinsert points one at a time at the largest hole found from 20000 random candidates followed by 100 steps of per-point minimax descent against the frozen other points; accept the reconstructed code under simulated annealing that allows temporary worsening up to +2e-4 with temperature decaying from 5e-5 to 0 over ~100s, then LogSumExp-refine. Maintain an archive keyed by a topology fingerprint (sorted contact degrees at 1e-6 plus the top 10 eigenvalues of the Gram matrix), reject or penalise children whose fingerprint is within a small distance of the record's fingerprint, and always restart surgery from the archived configuration with the most contacts among those within 5e-5 of the best score, so the search is forced to change basin topology rather than re-polish the same plateau.

idea: Epsilon-active tangent-space SQP/LP homotopy that linearises the plateau pairs and shrinks trust region and epsilon geometrically.
direction: Converge this basin properly with an epsilon-active-set SQP/LP homotopy instead of a $10^{-9}$-threshold LP. Work in per-point tangent coordinates (build a $13\times12$ null-space basis per point, 1188 variables), take as constraints all pairs with slack $<3\times10^{-6}$ (the visible plateau, roughly 600–900 pairs), and solve sequentially: minimise $t+\rho\|d\|^{2}$ subject to the linearised pair constraints $\le t$ and $\|d\|_\infty\le r$, starting at $r=3\times10^{-4}$ and shrinking $r$ geometrically to $10^{-8}$, after each step renormalising along the actual move and accepting only if the true max cosine decreases, while also shrinking the active-set epsilon (e.g. $\varepsilon\leftarrow\max(\varepsilon/3,10\,\text{slack spread})$) so plateau slacks are forced to collapse onto zero rather than merely being chased around. Use HiGHS with at most ~1200 constraints (keep the tightest), cap total LP time at ~110 s with an internal clock, and return the best iterate; success is diagnosed by the contact count at $10^{-9}$ jumping from 1 to hundreds and per-point maxima equalising, which would convert the $\sim10^{-6}$ plateau width into a real gain.

Search cyclic-rotation symmetric basins enumerating mixed orbit decompositions of 99 and optimise only orbit representatives with annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS from symmetrised-incumbent and random starts before releasing symmetry with full anneal and LP polish.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained basins beyond the C11/C9 tries, initialised by symmetrising the incumbent rather than from random representatives. Enumerate mixed orbit decompositions of 99 under a cyclic rotation action on five/six coordinate planes in $\mathbb{R}^{13}$ (plane angles $2\pi k/m$), e.g. $99=9\cdot11$, $11\cdot9$, $33\cdot3$, $49\cdot2+1$ (antipodal involution), $6\cdot16+3$, $8\cdot12+3$, allowing short orbits for points lying in fixed subspaces; for each candidate group, obtain starting representatives by averaging the rotations of the nearest points of `best.npy` (orthogonal symmetrisation/projection onto the orbit manifold) as well as a few random starts, optimise representatives only (at most $13\times$ #orbits variables) with analytic-gradient LogSumExp L-BFGS-B annealed over $\alpha=20\to200$, time-boxed to ~15 s per group and ~90 s total, then release the symmetry in stages (first allow the fixed coordinates, then all points) with a brief annealed full optimisation and wide-active LP polish. A symmetric or near-symmetric optimum automatically supplies the missing balanced contact graph, and the projection initialisation tests whether the record basin is a broken-symmetry version of such a code.

idea: Freeze 91-95 points and re-solve a 4-8 point plateau cluster by largest-hole insertion plus small tangent LP on freed points and near neighbours, with Metropolis acceptance and fallback to global best.
direction: Change the contact topology by low-dimensional block surgery rather than global shakes. From the plateau pairs (slack $<2\times10^{-6}$) form the near-contact graph, pick a connected cluster of 4–8 points that participate in many of the tightest pairs (plus, on alternate rounds, the two degree-1 points and their neighbours), freeze the other 91–95 points, and re-solve only the freed points: generate ~5000 random unit candidates plus local minimax refinements for each freed point against the frozen set (largest-hole insertion), then jointly polish just the freed points and their near neighbours (dot $>0.15$) with a small LP in at most $8\times12$–$20\times12$ tangent variables, which is cheap enough to run hundreds of times. Accept a surgery only after a short full LP polish if the true max improves, otherwise accept with a small Metropolis probability on the post-polish max to allow topology changes, cycle through different clusters for ~140 s, and always keep the global best as fallback—this directly creates and destroys contacts instead of perturbing all 99 points and sliding back.

Surgical rewiring of the unique max pair plus plateau-biased removals with greedy farthest-point reinsertion and subset annealed LogSumExp
direction: Rewire the topology by targeted surgery on the unique controlling pair and its plateau neighbourhood. Identify the argmax pair computationally, then repeat cycles that remove one endpoint of that pair together with two to six additional points sampled preferentially from points whose row maxima lie within \(10^{-5}\) of the global maximum; freeze the remaining points, generate at least 50,000 random sphere candidates, greedily insert replacements maximizing the minimum angular separation from the frozen set and from each other, and optimize only the inserted points plus neighbours within slack \(5\times10^{-6}\) using annealed LogSumExp with \(\alpha=100,500,2000\). Finish each cycle with a brief global polish, retain the result only if the exact score improves or the number of pairs within \(10^{-6}\) of the maximum materially decreases, otherwise revert to the checkpoint, and cap the whole procedure at roughly 20 cycles or 150 seconds.

idea: Gram-matrix feasibility search with alternating PSD-rank-13 and max-cosine projections over multiple targets and diverse initialisations, followed by annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS and tangent-LP polish.
direction: Ignore coordinates and attack feasibility for a target cosine via Gram-matrix alternating projections, to find a genuinely different basin. Fix a target $t$ (bisect over $t\in\{0.2445,0.2435,0.2425,0.241\}$) and iterate Douglas–Rachford/Dykstra projections of a $99\times99$ symmetric matrix between set A (PSD, unit diagonal, rank $\le13$, via eigendecomposition keeping the top 13 positive eigenvalues and resetting the diagonal) and set B (off-diagonal entries $\le t$, optionally also quantised toward a few allowed inner-product values to encourage a few-distance code), starting from the Gram matrices of `best.npy`, of random codes, and of structured lattice/spherical-design initialisations; each projection is a single $99\times99$ eigendecomposition, so thousands of iterations fit in ~60 s. If the residual $\|A-B\|$ stalls near zero, extract vectors from the top-13 factorisation, renormalise, and hand them to the annealed LogSumExp + LP polish; if a target proves infeasible, raise it and use the least-infeasible Gram matrix (rank-13 factorisation) as a novel starting code anyway, since its inner-product distribution—and hence contact topology—will differ from the record's plateau.

idea: Iterated basin-hopping with worst-point hole reinsertion plus fast annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS (no LP) to jump out of the single-pair plateau into a balanced basin.

Explore many random basins with annealed low-to-mid alpha per-point LogSumExp momentum descent and keep a structurally balanced elite by exact max plus per-point spread and contact counts, then polish only the top few with high-alpha descent and a time-bounded active-set trust-region LP.
direction: Generate genuinely different basins from random starts and select them by structural quality rather than by score alone. Run 30–60 inexpensive random initializations using batched Riesz-energy or low-\(\alpha\) LogSumExp gradient descent, with the exponent or \(\alpha\) annealed upward over a few hundred iterations, then evaluate each resulting configuration by its exact maximum, standard deviation of per-point maxima, number of contacts at thresholds \(10^{-5}\) and \(10^{-6}\), and dissimilarity from the incumbent after orthogonal alignment. Keep a small elite pool of configurations that are both low-scoring and structurally balanced—especially those with few rattlers and many near-contacts—polish only the best two or three with high-\(\alpha\) LogSumExp and a bounded active-set LP, and return the best exact result found; use strict per-stage deadlines so that exploration cannot consume the time reserved for final polishing.

idea: Targeted topological surgery on the unique max pair plus plateau neighbours with greedy maximin reinsertion and subset annealed LogSumExp.

idea: Active-set trust-region LP on the full 2e-6 plateau plus SVD null-space lateral moves with high-alpha LogSumExp polish to change basins.
direction: Perform a second-order, active-set descent of the entire near-contact plateau rather than polishing only the single maximum pair. Starting from `best.npy`, collect all pairs with slack below \(2\times10^{-6}\), build their tangent-space Jacobian, solve the trust-region LP minimizing \(t\) subject to every active linearized cosine being at most \(t\), and then compute an SVD of the active Jacobian to find near-null directions along which the plateau can move without first-order deterioration; test both signs of several such directions with step sizes \(10^{-4},3\times10^{-5},10^{-5}\), followed by a short high-\(\alpha\) LogSumExp polish. Add newly violated pairs after every accepted step, decrease the trust radius geometrically from \(3\times10^{-4}\) to \(10^{-7}\), accept only true decreases in the exact maximum, checkpoint the best configuration, and enforce a hard internal deadline of about 150 seconds with the incumbent as fallback.

idea: Active-set trust-region LP on the 2e-6 near-contact plateau plus SVD near-null moves and high-alpha LogSumExp polish.

idea: Force contacts into replicated families with reflection (49 mirrored pairs + fixed point for several flip sizes) and exact C11 (nine 11-orbits) symmetric manifolds optimized by annealed LogSumExp, then break symmetry with 1e-4/1e-3 shakes plus full polish and short LP.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained manifolds that force contacts to occur in replicated families instead of as one isolated pair. In particular, impose a reflection involution consisting of 49 point pairs \(\{y,Ry\}\), where \(R\) flips the signs of a selected subset of coordinates, plus one point fixed by \(R\); enumerate several flip patterns, optimize only the 49 representatives and the fixed point with annealed LogSumExp on the expanded 99-point configuration, and compare this with an exact cyclic \(C_{11}\) ansatz having nine 11-point orbits in six rotation planes plus one fixed coordinate. After optimizing each symmetric candidate, release the symmetry in stages by adding perturbations of size \(10^{-4}\) and \(10^{-3}\), followed by unconstrained LogSumExp and short LP polishing, while retaining the unperturbed symmetric optimum as a fallback; allocate bounded time to each symmetry pattern and return the best verified configuration.

idea: Basin-hopping with annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS plus largest-hole reinsertion and single-point greedy descent to escape the single-contact plateau.
Basin-hop with large shakes and void reinsertion of rattlers/overloaded points followed by annealed LogSumExp L-BFGS-B polish without LP to escape the single-contact plateau.
